title: Target Pair
statement: A warehouse scanner reports a list of package weights. Given a target weight, decide whether two different packages in the list weigh exactly the target together.
The two packages must be at different positions in the list. They may have the same weight, but a single package cannot be used twice.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers `n` and `target`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0] … a[n-1]`, separated by spaces.
outputFormat: Print `YES` if there are indices `i ≠ j` with `a[i] + a[j] = target`. Otherwise print `NO`.
constraints: A sum of two values can reach ±2·10^9, which overflows a signed 32-bit integer. Use a 64-bit type (long in Java/C#, long long in C++) for sums or differences.

examples.explanation: No two different values add up to 100.

private.complexity: O(n) expected time with a hash set of values seen so far; O(n log n) with sorting and two pointers. O(n^2) pair checking times out on the 200000-element hidden cases.
private.notes: Check target - a[i] against the set before inserting a[i], so a single element is never paired with itself.
